text.content:
Roll 1d8 or choose: the shadow haunting your days, and three questions you may always ask, answered honestly by the GM. From a certain point of view, your suffering is what lets you understand the world.

> Asking carries implications. If the amnesiac asks what memory this moment brings back, the GM cannot answer "none" — the moment does bring one back. In most games that's a table convention. In this world it is not. Attention shapes the Aether; at the margin, the question obliges the answer to exist. Whether it found the truth or made it is a question this game declines to settle.

| 1d8 | Torment | | Your questions | |:-:|---|---|---| | 1 | AMNESIA | You recall very little beyond your name and abilities. Every new memory carries relief… and trepidation | What happy or painful memory does this moment bring back? · Is there anyone here who remembers me, though I don't remember them? · Are they in control of their own actions? | | 2 | BETRAYAL | When someone needed you most, you ran. The blame lies entirely on your shoulders | Are they telling the truth? (reads deception, never error — the sincerely wrong ring true) · What is the best way out of here? · Who is the weakest target here? | | 3 | DEATH | Your hands are stained with blood, and you can never make your peace with it | What is the best way to hurt them? · What would make them lose control? · What here has killed before? | | 4 | WANT | You have been poor in the way that never leaves you | What is this worth, and to whom? · What does it cost to belong here? · Who here has never gone without? | | 5 | FRUSTRATION | Ambition and the fear of failure and judgment have turned you bitter and envious | What do they want the most? · Who do they serve? · What do they have that I don't? | | 6 | LOSS | You lost the people dearest to you, because you could not protect them. The guilt is a shackle | Who here is in the most danger? · What are we overlooking here? · What is most dangerous here? | | 7 | REVELATION | You glimpsed the true complexity of the world, and it shattered your values. You are painfully aware of your own ignorance | Where can I find that information? (a source — a place, a person, a book — never the answer itself) · What are their true feelings? · What is strange about this place? | | 8 | SOLITUDE | A lifetime of betrayal and manipulation has convinced you nobody finds you worthy of loyalty. A tool, not a person | What do they want from me? · How can I get them to do what I want? · What is the best place to hide? |

Your Torment is yours — it rides through every mask, and no Guise covers it. Establish what it means for your character when you take it, at the table.
